text: {"domain":"language acquisition","approachNotes":"You learn a language by understanding messages and being pushed to produce them. We’ll pair short comprehensible input — reading and listening slightly above your level — with small speaking and writing reps every session, so recognition becomes production. Grammar arrives as patterns you’ve already met in context, not as rules to memorize.","pitfalls":["App streaks that reward recognition without production","Grammar-first study that stalls real conversation","Input that is too hard, which quietly kills motivation"],"progressionPrinciples":["High-frequency conversational chunks before grammar rules","Comprehensible input at i+1, always paired with output","Recycle vocabulary across contexts rather than word lists"]}
